html:
Wattasid Morocco is the map's label for Morocco in 1530 and 1600. In 1530 the Wattasid sultans still ruled from Fez, though they were losing ground. By 1600 the label is out of date: Morocco then belonged to the Saadis.

In the early 16th century Portugal built forts along the Atlantic coast, at Agadir, Safi, Azemmour and Mazagan. The Wattasids could do little against them. In the south the Saadi dynasty, sharifs claiming descent from the Prophet, rallied the tribes to holy war, took Marrakesh in the 1520s and drove the Portuguese from Agadir in 1541.

The Saadis took Fez in 1549. The last Wattasid returned briefly with Ottoman help in 1554 but was killed the same year. The Saadi ruler Ahmad al-Mansur later grew rich after crushing a Portuguese army in 1578 and sent the expedition that won the Battle of Tondibi in 1591.
